## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl — one canonical class, currently
duplicated as `app-phone/src/main/java/com/mgilli/hyroxtracker/connectivity/permission/ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.kt`
and `app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/connectivity/permission/ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl.kt`

## Trigger

`ActivityBoundPermissionHost.bind()`, in each module, instantiates its
own module's `ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl` directly — observed
(`app-phone/.../connectivity/permission/ActivityBoundPermissionHost.kt`
line 24, `app-wear/.../connectivity/permission/ActivityBoundPermissionHost.kt`
line 56).

## Today

`ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl` exists once per application module,
with bodies identical except for the package declaration: same
constructor signature (`Activity`, `ActivityResultLauncher<String>`,
`SharedPreferences`), same `KEY_HAS_REQUESTED` constant, same four
overrides of `com.mgilli.core.domain.connectivity.ConnectivityPermissionSystem`
(`isGranted`, `canShowSystemPrompt`, `requestPermission`,
`openAppSettings`), same `onPermissionResult`. Each `ActivityBoundPermissionHost`
constructs its own module's copy. A change made to one — for instance
in `canShowSystemPrompt`'s handling of `KEY_HAS_REQUESTED` — leaves the
other module's copy untouched.

## Expected

One `ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl` is compiled once and used by
both `app-phone`'s and `app-wear`'s `ActivityBoundPermissionHost`, so a
correction made once reaches both modules.

Second gap — no module can hold it today. `ConnectivityPermissionSystemImpl`
wraps `Activity`, `ActivityResultLauncher` and `SharedPreferences`
(Android framework types), so it cannot move into `:core-domain`
(`core-domain/build.gradle.kts` applies the pure-Kotlin-JVM plugin only,
no Android dependency, per TECHNICAL_CONVENTIONS.md §3: "`:core-domain`
never imports anything from Android"). It cannot move into either
application module and be reused from the other either, since
TECHNICAL_CONVENTIONS.md §3 states "`:app-phone` and `:app-wear` never
import each other." `:core-sync` is the one existing module built as an
Android library (`core-sync/build.gradle.kts`, `android.library`
plugin) that both application modules could depend on for Android-typed
code, but §3 also states "Anything touching the device's OS —
permissions, sensors, preferences, Health Connect — lives in the
application module using it," which the class's current placement
follows and a shared home would contradict. Producing one implementation
serving both modules requires either placing it in an Android-capable
shared module (extending or repurposing `:core-sync`, or adding a new
one) or amending §3's placement rule for OS-permission code — neither
of which the gap names.
